intro_html: This sweet and sour pork is the meal-prep answer to your favorite Chinese takeout. Lean pork tenderloin cooks low and slow with peppers, onion, and pineapple in a honey soy glaze, then goes over rice. It runs a touch higher at around $4.98 a serving (at everyday cost), but you still get 55 grams of protein across 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $4.98 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings gives you 55 grams of protein at 581 calories with only 8 grams of fat.
upsell_html: Skip the delivery app and let this one prove homemade beats takeout on price and protein. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Tenderloin costs more than loin, so watch the sales. Buy tenderloin only when it drops below four dollars a pound and stock the freezer.
Canned pineapple in juice is cheaper than fresh and adds sweetness for free. Grab the canned pineapple in juice, not syrup, to skip the added sugar.
Bell peppers are cheapest in the multi-packs. Buy peppers by the bag when your store carries them that way.
make_it: Add the pork tenderloin, sliced peppers, and onion to the slow cooker.
Stir the honey, soy sauce, and pineapple with its juice together, then pour it over the top.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the pork is tender.
Cook the rice while the pork finishes.
Cut or shred the pork into bite-sized pieces and stir it back through the sauce.
Spoon the pork and vegetables over rice and drizzle with extra sauce.
